notes.notes: Temporarily removed debug camera until full functionality can be added.

notes.title: Central Update 7: The Hallway and Quality fixes
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43071434/3b2c372b3f0413035c53cf99243bb85e02e58da6.gif

Dear Employees,
This is a small patch addressing bugs and quality of life improvements. I figured I'd also unlock the current state of The Hallways for testing. In this patch:

Intro to The Hallways. This is a tricky area that's easy to get mixed up in.
Quality to life improvements which gives you a way to quickly get to different areas on the map if you die. 
Bug fix where inverting the controls wouldn't save.
Bug fix where outpost 3 and 4 achievements were swapped.
 Significant optimizations with regards to lighting.



Lastly,

I want to thank everyone who has played the game and especially those that gave feedback. It's been a tough year but we've been able to increase the frequency of updates and I think that's only going to increase going forward. Regardless, I genuinely appreciate the time you all have taken to report bugs and issues.

IG

notes.notes:

Major Update
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43071434/2cb624d67a83a3ef85fb44338b0f4f056acf2b7b.png
Dear Employees,
We Apologize for the delay in communications. Please be aware:

The area you're tasked with may have drastically increased in size. 
New rooms have been reported to us by numerous other employees and we are no longer accepting complaints. 
Fortunately, these seems to have decreased entity aggression.


Additionally, we've adjusted our algorithms to recognize interactions with entities (should they occur). This ensures employees get awarded achievements and proper compensations to the families.


As always,

Do not communicate or interact with any government personnel including the military. This is grounds for immediate termination.

notes.title: Update 5.1 Intro and Priorities
notes.notes:
I want to break character for a moment and address a harsh but fair criticism we received claiming this game is an asset flip. This is actually a very real problem on Steam and a lot of good developers can get pushed into obscurity by the volume of games getting released daily. This however is not an asset flip I'd like to take a moment to explain some of the work I've done, why it matters, and let you all decide for yourselves.

As a solo developer that primarily codes I am very much dependent of assets for things like models, animations, and textures. I do however put a lot of effort into modifying the assets for my specific use case and optimizations. The asset pack referenced is the Backrooms Horror Template. It is a great starting point for developers in the genre and I would highly recommend it but a significant amount of it has been modified to either add mechanics or improve performance. For context that specific asset pack has 580 unique files and 247 of them have been modified. Here is the git dif for reference:

Generally, textures are only going to be downsized where appropriate to save on memory and storage. Animations were modified to add trigger events like footsteps and improve collisions accuracy in the skeletal mesh. Meshes were modified to allow for procedural placement tools. Materials were modified to be either optimized (like walls and flooring) or added features like emissive being tied to the light intensity when flickering.

These changes alone don't necessarily mean I added value or uniqueness so let me also tell you about some of the mechanics, environments, and story elements added:


     There is an inventory system that was better exposed in through GUI in the last update. This GUI was removed until I could improve the quality, but the underlying system still remains and is vital to surviving as you can stockpile resources like fuel.
     System for barricading areas and repelling creatures. This is a difficult concept to implement sense the creatures in The Backrooms are aggressively offensive of your presence. So, if they see you directly, they will attach but they will also avoid your presence. This is currently implemented with the moveable lights to block passageways and openings. I do plan on implementing wall mounted cameras but there is still some work to do optimizing those. 
     I've built a player progress tracker that maps your location in real time as well as areas of interest and places you've died (which leaves a corpse behind). This will become much more useful as the levels grow as you'll be able to map out locations and reference points to navigate back to.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43071434/102c670f9386e81bc5143e5cacb3f18949c81f8f.png
     There is also a sneak mechanic where the 'leaning' ability comes into play with different creatures using different types of perception to see you (i.e. sight, sound, smell) but this is not in the key bindings as it is an axis input and not and action input.
     Physics actors and the ability to pick them up... lol, I know... but it's actually really well done. Objects have unique audio depending on whether it's getting hit, sliding, or rolling. It also used complex collision on concave surfaces so you can put cans inside of boxes. Idk, it's something I'm kind of proud of.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43071434/11187367c7f78987791d81c8386fc6ebad111daa.gif
     Additionally, I've put a ton of time into optimizations and features like local volumetrics, global illumination, interactive water, physics based interaction. Things that you'll see in AAA but I've been able to get running on the Steam Deck.
     I have also focused on building in-engine tools to help me build out environment faster. Whether those of dynamic lights to detect the ceiling height, water runoff that reacts with the ground, or simply parameter driven walls. These take time upfront but do help expedite development later on. I prefer this approach instead of a truly procedurally generated environment because it allows me to put custom touches on every aspect of the level design even as a solo developer.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43071434/761544cca0593064cdad6d05e7d25c1186869067.gif


There's a tone of other features I would like to add like fluid dynamics that can absolutely run on current gen hardware like fluid sims but it does take time to optimize, and I don't think it currently warrants the effort given to current state of the game.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43071434/817ac6a9ce5ac416dbe0e1c8a7f5633030efe0c8.gif

There's no doubt that this game has issues and is currently incomplete but I'm very satisfied with how development is going, and I firmly believe it's going to be a unique experience when it's done. Regardless, I think your criticism of the game is fair and accurate and I'm going to suspend work on the mechanics and features momentarily and focus my full efforts on the intro which is essentially a tutorial explaining all these mechanics as well as the core of the story.

All Employees,
We understand from our daily incident reports that the liminal spaces have become slightly more dangerous to our employees. As a company and a family we've decided to invest in our employee preparedness training. Going forward please enjoy these features:

 A Heads-Up-Display or HUD that reads your biometric vitals.
 An A.L.I.C.E. system outfitted on your biohazard suit for carrying gear and supplies
 A stabilizer for your body cam to reduce headbob and adjust FOV


As we learn more about the entities inside the rooms we will share that information directly with our staff and operators. Currently we know that these entities do not like to be seen. It's almost as though their existence in your consciousness is as uncomfortable to them as their appearance is to you. Anything from our side of the door (including your blood) will attract other... inhabitants.  

As your safety depends on it please remember:

 Lights will deter the inhabitants from entering areas but won't stop them once they're aware of you.
 Cameras can also help as a defense but you have to be monitoring them.
 Portable generators powering all your equipment require constant fuel.
 It is generally better to have the most minimal presence.
 Beware the water.

Welcome to The Backrooms! Thank you everyone for giving this game a chance.

 Lighting complexity on intro environment - apparently some of the equipment was causing the breakers to overload. This normally isn’t a problem but since the door to the real world unexpectedly shut we need to make sure everyone on our end it working.
Transition to the undefined environments - from the bodies we’ve found already, it seems to be random when victims noclip into the Backrooms but we still need to be sure to document anomalies we encounter.
Achievements - We know this job is tough and we want you to be rewarded on time for your efforts. We’ll keep working on our telecommunications system to ensure there’s no drops… even after you’ve passed on. 
Optimizations - We make every effort to ensure your equipment is up to date and running smoothly. We discovered some leaks in your suit when it gets wet. While they were never designed to be submersible we strive to keep you safe (and dry) whatever dimension you find yourself in.
